slides.title: Tell a clear story

children.text: Start with what your audience needs to understand.
Too much information makes the next step hard to see.
One message per slide, supported by a useful example.

slides.notes: Show the Comparison layout. Edit either card, preview the change, and use Undo to restore it. Ask the audience which message they would lead with.

slides.title: Show how it works

children.text: Turn a complicated process into three practical steps.
Choose your audience, message, and supporting content.
Use a short loop or guide the discussion manually.
Jump to a question, clarify details, and agree on next steps.

slides.notes: Demonstrate the Workflow layout. Explain that sections organize content, while loops select and order slides for playback. The main demo loop excludes Questions.

slides.notes: Open the Tables panel to edit a cell or add a row. Keep table text concise and inspect the footer clearance in the preview.

slides.title: Bring your content to life

children.text: Use a visual to support your message—not compete with it.
This sample image is included. Replace it with your own screenshot, diagram, or video.
Use a visual to support your message—not compete with it.
This sample image is included. Replace it with your own screenshot, diagram, or video.

slides.notes: Click Media beside the selected slide. Show the placement options, caption, sizing, and crop focus. The diagram is bundled and works offline. Videos are optional; commands and animations do not execute tasks.

slides.title: Walk through a task

children.text: Show a short command and explain its expected result.
SAFE EXAMPLE · DISPLAY AND COPY ONLY
Expected result: Hello, presentation! Nothing is executed by this presentation.
Show a short command and explain its expected result.
SAFE EXAMPLE · DISPLAY AND COPY ONLY
Expected result: Hello, presentation! Nothing is executed by this presentation.

slides.notes: Use the environment selector to switch between PowerShell and Bash. Copy the sample command. The studio only displays and copies text; execution happens outside the presentation.

slides.title: How do I make this presentation my own?

children.text: How do I make this presentation my own?
Replace the sample text, add your logo and media, and choose a theme. Export an editable ZIP to keep a complete copy.
Open Edit, choose a slide, and change its heading. Your browser saves a recovery draft.
How do I make this presentation my own?
Replace the sample text, add your logo and media, and choose a theme. Export an editable ZIP to keep a complete copy.
Open Edit, choose a slide, and change its heading. Your browser saves a recovery draft.

slides.notes: Open Questions from Sections or press Q. Then choose Browse Questions or press B. Explain that more questions can be added to this section and searched by topic.

slides.title: Make it yours

children.text: Customize your story. Save a complete copy. Open it wherever you present.
Project → Export keeps your slides, media, notes, and recovery history together.
Customize your story. Save a complete copy. Open it wherever you present.
Project → Export keeps your slides, media, notes, and recovery history together.

slides.notes: Close by demonstrating the Project → Export menu. Editable ZIP is the durable handoff; browser drafts are local recovery copies. Presentations opens recent projects and external ZIP files.
